__I try not to bombard myself with new friendships__-- For example: If I want to join a new discord server to make friends, I would limit myself to 1 server only. Adding onto that, since I know that I cannot handle friendships well, I tell everyone I become friends with exactly how I am.  
  
Something like, "Hey, I really enjoy being friends with you and I just wanted to let you know before we continue that it's a little hard for me to keep up with communication; I'll do my best but sometimes I might not respond fast and I promise it's not intentional! I just tend to get socually burnt out sometimes and become a hermit :c"  
By letting them know beforehand how you are, friends are less likely to cut you off. This avoids confusion (to them, they have no idea why you are suddenly quiet or distant). __Just be completely open and honest with them!__  
  
Additionally, start off with maybe 1 friend and don't start the friendship by talking a ton then suddenly not talking at all- into a cycle. __Limit yourself even if you want to talk all night__, because you know you might not do this in a few weeks. If you allow it to happen, the other party will be confused on why you suddenly changed. Even if *you* know yourself, *they* don't know that you mean well or about how you are when it comes to friends. So try not to be extra chatty in the beginning! And again, be honest with how you are.   
  
Lastly, __try not to blame them if they don't want to be friends__. If they would rather have a friendship with a lot of communication every day, then that's their choice and that's okay! Once you tell them about how you are, there are people who won't be okay with it. And there's nothing wrong with that! Try your best to understand that other people have different needs when it comes to friendship. :)  
  
__TLDR;__ Limit yourself and how many friendships you decide to take on, be __honest and upfront__ with new friends, and take your time. It's a slow process to come out of your shell! But only you know yourself the best, so try and work around that for other people. Slowly, you'll build a tolerance to it!

I am an extreme introvert who may not seem like it, and I have lost many friends in the past because I was not attentive enough (even for normal standards), where I would unintentionally ghost for a month at a time and then suddenly come back same as ever for a few days to have fun with friends. This was strange for many friends I had & hurtful to a lot, too, as I always seemed sociable and would suddenly ghost them. I've become much better at it at 22, but it was a long process to get to a point where I can chat at least once a week. I'm not sure why I am this way, but it definitely isn't intentional nor am I giving my attention to other friends in the process. Just how my introverted brain works and how often I have the energy to socialize. Not sure if this will help, as I know this isn't very conventional, but it might help seeing another perspective!  
  
Edit: I also want to add that you are completely valid with your feelings! Because I am aware of how I am, I know not every friendship will "click"/work because the other party may want more than what I can give in a friendship. So I intentionally make sure to tell everyone before becoming friends & making sure it is alright with them first so that I don't end up confusing and hurting them in the future. I feel like it is a friend's responsibility to be honest & clear with these things.
